(12 April 2000) |attendance=11,677,585{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co91/se3244/attendance/ |title=Premier League 1999/2000 » Attendance » Home matches |website=WorldFootball.net |access-date=6 January 2024 }} |average attendance=30,730 |prevseason=[[1998–99 FA Premier League|1998–99]] |nextseason=[[2000–01 FA Premier League|2000–01]] }} The '''1999–2000 FA Premier League''' (known as the '''FA [[Carling brewery|Carling]] Premiership''' for sponsorship reasons) was the eighth season of the [[Premier League|FA Premier League]], and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] secured their sixth Premiership title. Like the [[1998–99 FA Premier League|previous season]], they lost only three league games all season. Unlike in the 1998–99 season, they won by a comfortable margin – 18 points as opposed to a single point. Manchester United lost their defence of the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] following a 3–2 defeat against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the quarter-finals. The club had withdrawn from the [[1999–2000 FA Cup]] to participate in the [[FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA World Club Championship]] at the request of the FA who wanted Manchester United to compete to support England's bid to host the [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]]. [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] won the last FA Cup held at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] before its redevelopment. The [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] final was won by [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]], for the second time in four seasons. In Europe, [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] reached the [[UEFA Cup]] semi-final and [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] were on the losing side to Galatasaray in the [[2000 UEFA Cup final|UEFA Cup final]]. Only one newly promoted team suffered relegation: [[Watford F.C.|Watford]], who finished in last place, and achieved a then record Premiership low of just 24 points (a record since broken by multiple teams), despite a decent start to their campaign which saw them beat both Liverpool (at Anfield) and Chelsea. The most successful promoted team was [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]], who finished seventh in the final table and spent much of the season pushing for a place in European competition. [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]], back in the top division for the first time since 1922, secured their Premiership survival on the last day of the season with a 1–0 win over [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]. The result meant that Liverpool lost out on a [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] place, and [[Wimbledon F.C.|Wimbledon]] were relegated after 14 years of top-division football. Second-from-bottom [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] were relegated in their penultimate game of the season, having spent 15 of the previous 16 seasons in the top division. Wednesday's season included an 8–0 defeat at [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle]]. Amazingly [[Coventry City]] went all season without an away win but still managed to secure 14th place due to an impressive home record which saw them win 12 out of their 19 matches. As well as Premiership champions Manchester United and runners-up Arsenal, third placed Leeds United qualified for the 2000–01 Champions League. UEFA Cup places went to fourth placed Liverpool, F.A Cup winners Chelsea, and League Cup winners Leicester City. Promoted to the Premiership for 2000–01 were [[Football League First Division|First Division]] champions [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]], runners-up Manchester City and playoff winners [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]]. For the first time since the formation of the Premiership, all of the promoted teams had been members of the Premiership before. ==Teams== Twenty teams competed in the league – the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[1998–99 Football League First Division|First Division]]. The promoted teams were [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]], [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]] and [[Watford F.C.|Watford]], who returned after absences of two, seventy-seven and eleven years respectively. This was also both Bradford City and Watford's first season in the Premier League. They replaced [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]], [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] and [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]], who were relegated to the [[1999–2000 Football League First Division|First Division]]. Charlton Athletic and Nottingham Forest were immediately relegated after a season's presence, while Blackburn Rovers' seven-year top flight spell came to an end. ===Stadiums and locations===
